description:
No spec subject — bookkeeping epic.

Impromptu epic created 2026-07-26 to land four independently-surfaced follow-up tickets on a SINGLE PR. Children were each carved by an earlier ticket's cold verification or critical review and had no owning epic (gai was reparented here from specled_-xkn; xkn retains its other three children).

Children and the subjects they advance:
  - specled_-48i  specled.package      content-lint verification for adoption_guide/concepts_guide must requirements
  - specled_-vk0  specled.package      doc-identifier lint hardening (lookbehind bounds, severity-corpus asymmetry, digit codes, stale-marker sweep, two-way mirror)
  - specled_-gai  specled.spec_review  retire duplicated coverage_tab_bind_closure compound statement, repoint lib/** covers markers
  - specled_-ymn  specled.verification cross_vm_temp_names ADR vs hash_store fixed-name .tmp sibling; tracer pid-separation falsifiability; ADR affects: reach

Sequencing rationale: 48i and vk0 both edit .spec/specs/package.spec.md (48i the adoption_guide/concepts_guide verification entries, vk0 the decisions: list plus must wording), so 48i blocks vk0 to avoid a real same-file merge conflict. gai and ymn touch disjoint specs and lib files and run concurrently with 48i.

Orchestrated by /orchestrate-epic. Implementers: Codex. Verify/audit/rebase: Claude.

- [stale-spec] A SUPERSEDING ADR must carry forward every normative clause of the ADR it replaces — prohibitions AND carve-outs. Dropping a carve-out silently narrows policy, and dropping a prohibition silently widens it; neither is visible to `spec.check`. Diff the old Decision section against the new one clause by clause (from specled_-ymn, which dropped the very test-only carve-out its own Out of Scope relied on)
- [other] Extend an ADR's `affects:` only for subjects whose DOMAIN the decision governs — never because a shared surface file (e.g. verifier.ex) happens to appear on that subject's `surface:` list. Surface coincidence makes the spec graph assert something false, which is the mirror image of under-claiming reach. Prove necessity by removing the entry and re-running the gate (from specled_-ymn)
- [other] Collapsing duplicated narration to a one-line pointer is only safe if the pointer TARGET actually contains the specifics being removed. Verify the target AFTER the edit; a commit that trims sites and genericises the target at the same time destroys the rationale it claims to centralise (from specled_-ymn)

A grader's unproven negative can regress a green gate through an audit into the implementer's work (from specled_-ymn)
- [other] `branch_guard_missing_subject_update` fires on SURFACE membership and test-tag impact, independently of realization binding — so regenerating `.spec/realization_hashes.json` cannot green it, and a subject can be dragged into the impacted set by an edit as trivial as a comment trim. Check `mix spec.next --base origin/main` for the authoritative co-change list before reverting a subject spec (from specled_-ymn)

(Supersedes all earlier LESSONS comments on this epic; this is the current full list.)

LESSONS (additions from specled_-gai verify pass 2; full list continues from the prior LESSONS comment)
- [untested-clause] Prose you NEWLY AUTHOR into a requirement is subject to the falsifiability gate exactly like code. specled_-gai fixed an unfalsifiable `must` by writing a concrete statement — and two clauses of the NEW statement ("sorted reached_files, sorted unreached_files") could not fail. Falsify EVERY clause of a statement you write, one mutation per clause; proving the cheapest clause (a separate function head) says nothing about the data-shape clauses beside it (from specled_-gai)
- [untested-clause] An ORDER or SORTEDNESS clause is unfalsifiable when every fixture holds a single-element collection — order is unobservable, so `Enum.sort(:desc)` passes. Before asserting sortedness in a requirement, confirm some fixture has >= 2 elements in that collection (from specled_-gai)
- [other] `append_only` blocks deleting a requirement id (`append_only/requirement_deleted`, append_only.ex:114-137) unless an authorizing `.spec/decisions/` ADR resolves it — so "just delete the empty requirement" is NOT available to a ticket whose Allowed touches exclude `.spec/decisions/`. Conversely `detect_must_downgraded` compares only MODAL CLASS, so a full statement rewrite that keeps "shall" is invisible to the guard. Rewriting a requirement in place is the guard-legal move, which is exactly why the NO-ORPHANED-CONTRACT gate must be run by hand (from specled_-gai; the audit's recommended "delete the umbrella" end state was unachievable and the implementer was right to reject it)

overlap in this epic and warrants explicit confirmation.

LESSONS (additions from specled_-ymn audit pass 2)
- [other] When a gate-greening co-change would require asserting something FALSE in the spec graph, drop the low-priority change that provoked it instead of buying the green with a false assertion. specled_-ymn's L-severity comment trim in verifier.ex dragged specled.prose_guard into the branch-guard impacted set purely by surface membership; reverting the trim was correct and adding a prose_guard link would have re-committed the exact over-claim the ticket was bounced for. Trade away cosmetic scope, never spec truth (from specled_-ymn)
- [other] A subject->ADR `decisions:` link that the ADR's `affects:` does NOT reciprocate is gate-clean but is an UNDER-claim on the ADR side. When a subject genuinely owns code the ADR governs, wire BOTH directions; only skip the ADR side when the subject does not actually belong, in which case skip the subject side too. Gate-cleanliness is not the test — reciprocity of a true claim is (from specled_-ymn)
- [other] A universal reach claim in an ADR ("names EVERY subject that ...") is a standing liability: specled_-ymn's was false three different ways across two iterations. Prefer enumerating the surfaces the ADR governs plus an explicit bullet for each deliberate exclusion and why, over a universal quantifier no one can keep true (from specled_-ymn)

SCOPE REDUCTION RECORDED — not silent, and not a /descope invocation (that requires the user).
specled_-ymn's F2/CF2 item (trim the three re-narrated cross-VM rationale comments in
lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex to one-line pointers, L severity) was implemented in iteration 1
and is being REVERTED in iteration 3. Cause: any verifier.ex edit re-opens
branch_guard_missing_subject_update against specled.prose_guard, which carries that file on
its surface despite prose guarding having nothing to do with temp names, and prose_guard binds
no code there so no realization-attestation downgrade exists. The only alternative was
asserting that a temp-naming ADR governs prose_guard — the same over-claim iteration 1 was
bounced for. Carved to specled_-chb (P4) with the full constraint analysis, including the
observation that the more valuable fix is prose_guard's whole-file surface claim on a
3800-line general-purpose module, not the cosmetic trim itself. Surfaced to the user.
